 O R D E R
1.
Leave granted.

2. On the complaint made by the appellant, FIR/Crime No.0253 dated 06.06.2024 has been registered at Police Station Jait, Mathura under Sections 147, 376, 377, 354, 342, 323, 506 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

Another FIR No.0334 dated 22.09.2024 has also been registered at Police Station Narkhi, District Firozabad under Sections 318(4), 338, 336(3) and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

3. As per the contents of the FIR, the appellant alleged that she had been forcibly taken away by respondent No. 2 in or about September 2017 and was wrongfully confined for a prolonged period extending till October 2023, during which she was subjected to repeated sexual assault, including rape and unnatural offences, along with physical assault and criminal intimidation.
Respondent No.2, at the relevant time, was 52 years old or so, and the appellant was 19 years old.
NITIN TALREJA Date: 2026.04.01

16:57:53 IST Reason:
4. The FIR further discloses that multiple accused persons, including associates and family members of respondent No. 2, were involved in the commission of the offences, and that the appellant was kept under coercion and threat during the entire period.

It is further alleged that some false and fabricated documents showing marriage between the parties at Arya Samaj Temple in Village Kotla,
District Firozabad were also relied upon by the respondent-accused in order to escape the consequences.

5. It is equally important to mention at this stage that the appellant was allegedly abducted in the night when her mother was alleged to have been gangraped by the respondent No. 2 and his associates.
Another allegation in the FIR is that the wife of respondent No.2 (Smt. Kamlesh) and other individuals are also involved in the crime.

sentences.text:
On the other hand, the case of respondent No.2 appears to be that he lost his wife in the year 2006 and that he was a widower when he entered into a consensual relationship with the appellant;
they both married and a girl child was also born from the wedlock in 2018.
The child is currently six years old and is in custody of the appellant-mother.
7. Taking prima facie notice of these facts that the High Court vide impugned order(s) has released the respondent No. 2 on regular bail, the aggrieved appellant is before us.
8. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused some of the documents.

It is neither expedient nor feasible to go into the rival factual contentions as the issues such as whether the respondent No. 2 was a widower and eligible to perform second marriage or whether there was a consensual relationship between the parties and the child was born out of a lawful wedlock etc.
would essentially require factual evidence.
Moreover, the appreciation of such evidence is best reserved for trial.

9. Since the appellant has categorically denied entering into any marriage with respondent No.2 and has further alleged that all the documents relied upon by him are forged and fabricated, and has further expressed the apprehension that respondent No.2 is threatening her to take away the child from her custody, we dispose of these appeals with the following directions:
i. Respondent No. 2, or any person acting on his behalf, shall not initiate or pursue any proceedings, nor take any steps, directly or indirectly, to obtain custody of the minor child until the question regarding the status and relationship of the parties is adjudicated by a court of competent jurisdiction;

ii. Without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the parties, and in view of the admitted position of respondent No. 2 that the child was born from the relationship in question, respondent No. 2 is directed to pay a sum of 40,000/- per month towards the maintenance, education, and overall welfare of the minor child.
The said amount shall be deposited in the bank account of the appellant on or before the 10th day of each calendar month;
iii. The aforesaid payment shall not be construed as an admission of any marital relationship between the parties, nor shall it create any equities in favour of respondent No. 2;

iv. Any default in payment, or any attempt by respondent No. 2 to interfere with the custody of the child or to intimidate the appellant, her family members, or any witnesses, shall be treated as misuse of the concession of bail.

In such an event, it shall be open to the High Court to take appropriate action, including cancellation of bail;
v.
The Station House Officer, Police Station Narkhi, District Firozabad, shall maintain strict vigil over the conduct of respondent No. 2.
In case of any complaint or material indicating threat, intimidation, or interference, an appropriate report shall be forthwith submitted to the jurisdictional High Court for necessary action.
